LESSON: READING 1.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORIES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you predict the outcome of a story even before you read it? 2. How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words in a story?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. outline the sequence of events in a short story that they have read,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use contextual clues to infer the meanings of words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. answer direct and inferential questions from a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge the role of reading in communication. ● In groups, guide learners with low vision, to predict the events by reading the title and observing illustrations. SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking as the learner assesses the relationship between their own lives and those of the characters in the story.

● Citizenship as the learner cites issues on human rights.

Values:
Responsibility as the learner takes different roles to dramatise the events in the story.

Link to other subjects:

Inferring contextual meanings of words based on the events in the story, is linked to critical thinking in Social Studies.

(Life Skills Education)
